headline: US Centcom: five Iranian oil tankers hit (one sunk); Iran rockets Jordan and claims Gulf ship strikes. OpenAI posts a Navier–Stokes Millennium claim; Weisweiler grid-saboteur arrest.

stories.title: US hits five Iranian oil tankers; Iran rockets Jordan / claims Gulf strikes

facts.text: tagesschau / SPIEGEL (Wed AM): Centcom says it “destroyed” five IRGC-linked crude tankers — M/T Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, Riesco (sunk) in the Gulf of Oman, plus M/T Derya near Kharg — after crews were told to leave.
Framed as retaliation for IRGC ballistic-missile attacks on a US warship over the prior two days (ship unhit; no US casualties claimed).
Jordan: Petra — air defenses intercept 18 of 20 Iranian ballistic missiles; two fall in uninhabited areas; no injuries reported. IRGC claims hits on Al-Azraq / US jet basing (unverified).
Overnight IRGC statement (Irna): also claims attacks on US ships and tankers/freighters in Hormuz; warns Kuwait/Bahrain-port tankers to evacuate — independent verification incomplete.
Context: Saturday Centcom already claimed three earlier tanker strikes; Hormuz shipping remains the pressure point in the wider Iran conflict.

stories.whyItMatters: Biggest overnight escalation in the tanker/Hormuz track — oil logistics and Jordan basing in the same news cycle.

stories.title: OpenAI: Navier–Stokes Millennium claim via ~10k-agent run

facts.text: OpenAI (8 Sep): analytical proof + Lean formalization that 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes can blow up in finite time (Clay C/D) — inward-spiraling vortex, smooth force, finite energy.
Internal model “significantly more capable than GPT‑6 Astra”; ~10k concurrent agents in the NS group; ~2.7M messages / ~130B output tokens; ~88h to resolution + 17h Lean via GPT‑6 Astra.
Also resolved unforced Euler regularity (~100 agents / ~50h). OpenAI says it will not claim the Millennium Prize.
Update vs yesterday’s Buckmaster/OpenAI Euler fight: OpenAI publishes full NS writeup; recognizes Alpöge/Buckmaster priority on forced Euler; claims no prior access to their work.

stories.whyItMatters: If the Lean check holds peer review, it’s a frontier-math milestone and a public capability flex — afternoon’s Euler fight just got a bigger sibling.

stories.title: Weisweiler: alleged grid saboteur Daniel V. arrested with explosives

facts.text: tagesschau / n-tv (Tue): police detain 48-year-old Daniel V. (Gevelsberg) near Kraftwerk Weisweiler / Hambach area — Cottbus warrant; no resistance.
Cologne police: explosives on his person; further charges found at a tent in undergrowth; EOD reviewing. Reul: “wollte weitermachen… Einzeltäter.”
Method alleged across NRW/Brandenburg/Saxony: homemade rockets firing conductive wire onto HV lines — short circuits at Bergheim (units offline days) and Turnow-Preilack / Jänschwalde (no blackout).
Confession letters cite fight against fossil power (“Stromerzeugung aus fossilen Brennstoffen ist ein Verbrechen”); Dobrindt: “Klimaextremismus.” Mon: more launchers + letter found at Weisweiler.

stories.whyItMatters: Closes the multi-state manhunt that filled last week’s briefs — arrest next to the latest Weisweiler devices.

stories.title: CISA/NSA/FBI: China AI firms’ industrial-scale distillation

facts.text: Joint advisory AA26-251A (8 Sep): DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, Z.AI accused of industrial-scale distillation from US frontier models since ≥late 2024.
Claims billions of tokens / millions of requests; gray-market “transfer stations,” bulk premium subs, CoT extraction; DeepSeek R1/V3 and Alibaba Qwen named as beneficiaries.
Urges anomalous-usage detection, response degradation for suspected distillers, and cross-provider intel sharing.

stories.whyItMatters: Puts a sealed USG label on the distillation arms race — compliance and API abuse detection become board topics overnight.

stories.title: Google: DMA search changes are “biggest degradation” in 29 years

facts.text: heise: Google rolls DMA Search UI changes across the EEA — hotel/flight/rail/product queries elevate third-party aggregators (Expedia, Booking); users can switch provider.
Nick Fox (Google): calls it “the biggest degradation” of Search quality in 29 years; non-EU users unaffected. Prior DMA tweaks allegedly cut some service bookings ~30%.
Context: late-July Commission fines totaling €890M DMA breaches — €460M tied to self-preferencing in Search.

stories.whyItMatters: Europe’s Search chrome changes in the wild — expect screenshots and local SEO churn this week.

facts.text: UK ATC (NATS) flight-processing outage Tue hit Heathrow/Gatwick and more; hundreds of cancellations — recovery continuing Wed (BBC / CNA).
Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quits with X/WSJ blast: builders “earnestly believe” AI could kill us by decade-end; race dynamics force risk-taking (heise).
Ricoh/Pentax: current K-series DSLRs discontinued; company teases a “new stage” DSLR concept later (PetaPixel).
DeepMind AlphaGenome Atlas: precomputed regulatory impact of ~9B single-nucleotide variants (~1 PB) + AVI score for researchers (Google blog 8 Sep).
Kyiv Independent: Tue missile/drone wave after US-envoy pause — ≥5 killed, ~70 injured nationwide; capital hard hit.
